source: the raw records of the runners of GitHub, judged again with the catalog after the calibration of the propagation

cells.name: iptables, callers learn that a shared dependency flaps: endpoints only

prediction.text: The algebra predicts that the Service has no ready endpoint, and that the rules of each node have no backend. The band is 12 s to 26.105 s after the fault. Redis is black-holed 3 times for 27 s, with a rest of 15 s from each heal to the next fault. The heal comes 0 s–0.5 s after the hold. Each request needs Redis, thus each request fails from each fault until the callers recover. Each connection of A stays open on its replica, thus it gets the 503 of the service at the trip of the latch, and no refusal. The kubelet and the propagation remove both replicas 12 s–26.105 s after each fault, thus the Service is empty in each fault. A succeeds on its open connections when the readiness of the service recovers, up to 9.26 s after the heal. Each recovery ends before the next fault. One success resets the readiness debounce, the kubelet probe and the retry window of the client of Redis. Thus each fault is the same as the first one. Each client sends a request each 20 ms, thus approximately 3852–5517 requests fail in each fault, and 11556–16551 in the run.

cells.why: Each of the 3 counted runs agrees with the prediction. The median is 19.941 s. The counted runs measured 17.669 s to 20.211 s.
